rationale:
I judge the reviewed tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection`. Each obligation maps to at least one marked test with assertions that enforce it. I did not request implementation source.

- **Resolving a selector from the root against the retained outline.**
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` selects every outline item by its selector. For each one it asserts that the text equals the item's span and that `structural_hash` matches.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` selects with `second.select(main)`. A handle that is already a selection therefore resolves from the file's root.
  - The same test covers percent-encoded names, `#N` duplicates and anonymous `section@`/`block@` segments.
  - `css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent` selects `rule[a%20b]#1` and `#2` and `media[print]#2/rule[a]`, and checks that the content differs.
  - The empty selector is tested in `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` (`selected.select("")` gives the root id and full text).
- **Owned result that shares the snapshot and fingerprinting rules.**
  - `std::ptr::eq(second.outline(), contents.outline())` and the `function.outline()` check show that the snapshot is shared.
  - `explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme` shows that a selection keeps the custom fingerprint scheme and `structural_hash`. It also shows that a newer scheme changes the fingerprint.
  - `formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans` shows that `text()` on a selection is the raw, pre-redaction text, while `format()` is redacted.
- **No additional file read, and usable after the original handle is dropped.**
  - In `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits`, `drop(file)` and an on-disk rewrite are followed by assertions that the selected text and fingerprint are unchanged. `OutlineContent::from_id` then fails, but `selected.select("")` still returns the original `"first\nsecond\n"`. That shows `select` does not re-read the file.
- **Attached source and `id()`/`text()` semantics.**
  - The Rust test asserts that the selected function text starts with the `///` doc comment and contains `#[inline]`.
  - The `id()` assertions are in the outlive test.
- **Identical plain-text lines are interchangeable.**
  - `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` selects the duplicated `alpha` line selector and gets `"alpha"`.
  - `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` selects the duplicate `same` line selector and gets `"same"`.
- **Errors.**
  - `missing_file_and_invalid_selections_are_errors` asserts an error for a malformed selector (`fn[`) and for a missing item (`fn[absent]`).
  - `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` asserts an "ambiguous" error for duplicate non-line kinds. It also asserts one for `line` items whose hashes differ.
  - The CSS test asserts that an unnumbered `rule[a%20b]` among duplicates is an error.

Only one malformed-selector form is tested. A missing `#N` index is also untested. Both fall in classes that are already exercised, so I don't count them as gaps. The text names no further boundary for them.

text: :::{req} selection
`OutlineContent::select` resolves a selector from the file's root against the
retained outline. It returns another owned `OutlineContent` for that item,
sharing the original source snapshot and fingerprinting rules. Selection
performs no additional file read and remains usable after the original handle
is dropped. Resolution follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, including its rule that
identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. Invalid, missing, or ambiguous
selections return an error under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
/// Select an item from this retained file snapshot.
pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
/// Address of the selected item.
pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineId;
/// Original selected text, including attached source, before redaction.
pub fn text(&self) -> &str;
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} errors
File-read and parsing failures return errors, distinct from successful contents
for an empty file. Selecting a language commits to that language's parsing
rules; a parse failure is reported rather than interpreted as plain text.
A malformed selector, a missing item, or an ambiguity not permitted by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` also returns an error.
